The Mecklenburg-Schwerin Minister to Copenhagen had given a lunch for the philologists in Berlin, and at that time all of the philologists were utterly German – Wilhelm von Ofterdingen was the exception. Anyway, the lunch was a huge event in Berlin, because each philologist was very shy and only looked at his glass of water when nobody was paying attention to him. David Jones, as always, sat there and held forth and also there was a great press all about the meeting of the minds between Jones and the genius of Mecklenburg
